metadata.$comment: schema_version tracks the CID JSON schema revision. oac_spec_revision tracks the OAC Base Specification revision this OAC was designed against.
metadata.description: <Human-readable description of this OAC CID instance>
metadata.$comment_pct: platform_token: optional. Vendor-defined interoperability validation token for co-designed/co-validated closed platform deployments. Requires iana_pen to also be present — platform_token shall not appear without iana_pen. See spec Section 7.2.1.
metadata.$comment_pen: iana_pen: optional integer. IANA Private Enterprise Number of the organization responsible for this CID. Required when platform_token is used. May be declared independently of platform_token. See spec Section 7.2.2.

primary.$comment: input_voltage: nominal primary rail. Allowed values: '+12V', '+50V'. connector_type: primary power connector variant per OCP OAC Base Spec v0.9 Section 9.3 -- '100A' (BK100, 80A derated, all form factors) or '125A' (BK125, 100A derated, double-wide only). OPL fields define Operational Power Levels per OCP OAC Base Spec v0.9 Section 10.1.2. opl_max_w and opl_emg_w are required. opl_eff_w, opl_red_w, and opl_set_min_w are optional. opl_set_min_w declares the floor of the configurable OPL-SET range; the ceiling is always opl_max_w and is not declared separately. Ordering constraint: opl_max_w >= opl_eff_w >= opl_red_w >= opl_emg_w.

power.$comment_excursion: excursion: optional array, 2 to 8 entries, interval_us strictly ascending. Each entry declares the maximum ratio of average power over an interval of that length to opl_max_w. ratio_max is normalized to opl_max_w only -- it does not rescale at OPL-EFF, and the effective ratio is 1 at OPL-RED, OPL-EMG, and OPL-SET. Each ratio_max must be >= 1.0 and must not exceed the OCP OAC Base Spec v0.9 Section 10.1.4 envelope at that interval. That envelope is piecewise: R = 3 for T <= 100, R = 4 - 0.2171 * ln(T) for 100 < T < 1000000, R = 1 for T >= 1000000, and ratios must be monotonically non-increasing as interval_us rises. The intervals below are the recommended grid of spec Table 7.3.2-2; the ratios below are placeholders at the Section 10.1.4 ceiling and should be replaced with this OAC's characterized values. Delete the whole excursion array if this OAC is not characterized -- absence means uncharacterized, and the controller will budget at the Section 10.1.4 ceiling. See spec Section 7.3.2.

connectors.$comment: Populated connector template. 'id' must be unique and one of: CONN0-CONN6, CABLE. CONN0 must always appear first with populated=true. connector_profile is optional. Use an OCP-ratified profile identifier (prefix 'OAC-PROF-'). When connector_profile is set, high_speed_lanes, clocking, and discrete_signals must be omitted from this connector object -- they are defined entirely by the profile. Omit connector_profile entirely to define signals explicitly. mpesti_capable is required on CONN0 and must be omitted on CONN1-CONN6 and CABLE: it declares whether CONN0 Pin A1 is additionally overloaded with M-PESTI. Presence detection itself (the GND tie on Pin A1) is fixed by the OAC Base Specification and is never declared in the CID.

lanes.$comment: One object per physical lane-direction pair. List all RX entries (ascending lane_index) first, then all TX entries.

clocking.$comment: One entry per reference clock signal. Use pin_positive and pin_negative for REFCLK_DIFF; use pin for REFCLK_SINGLE. ssc_supported is required.

discrete_signals.$comment: One entry per discrete sideband signal. Vendor-defined signals must use the VENDOR_ prefix. Active-low signals must end with #. pullup_required and pulldown_required are mutually exclusive.

connectors.$comment: Unpopulated connector stub. Use this pattern for any connector position that is physically absent on this OAC variant. Only 'id' and 'populated' are needed.
